problem: pack now writes the streams in reverse order (3,2,1,0) while the length table still describes streams 0-2 and there is no version marker, so the byte layout no longer matches main and the two layouts cannot be told apart.
unpack reads the new reversed layout, so blocks produced by main (and branch blocks read by main) decode to wrong data without raising any error.
The module now imports the reference copy reference_impl when it loads, so importing fourstream fails with ModuleNotFoundError wherever that file is not shipped alongside it.
The stream-length limit is read from _ref.MAX_TABLE_LENGTH instead of the module's own MAX_TABLE_LENGTH, which is now unused, leaving two sources for a limit tied to the 2-byte table field.
The literal 6 replaces TABLE_SIZE at lines 38, 41, 43 and 45, so the checks and offsets would not follow a change to the table size.
Error messages at lines 27, 31, 39 and 42 dropped the counts and lengths main reported, which makes failures harder to diagnose.
The branch changes the byte layout of pack/unpack with no test that checks known output bytes or that main-encoded blocks still decode, which is how F1/F2 went unnoticed.
